paragraphs: Test-time adaptation adjusts a trained model to the data it encounters during use. Many existing methods do this by updating normalization layers. The paper identifies two weaknesses in that approach: small batches can produce unstable normalization statistics, and adaptation remains tied to the pretrained model’s structure and training statistics. These weaknesses become especially relevant when deployment data differ substantially from training data.

The proposed alternative introduces a Buffer layer as the component used for adaptation while preserving the pretrained backbone. This changes where adaptation happens: the original model parameters remain intact, reducing the risk that adapting to new inputs will erase previously learned capabilities. The Buffer layer is also designed as a modular addition that can work within nearly all existing test-time adaptation frameworks.

The authors report improved robustness to domain shifts and strong resistance to forgetting in their experiments. They also find consistent improvements across different architectures. The contribution is therefore both an adaptation mechanism and a reusable component for strengthening existing adaptation methods.
neurips-2025-buffer-layers-for-test-time.tldr: Buffer layers adapt models to new test data while preserving the pretrained backbone, improving robustness and resistance to forgetting in experiments.

paragraphs: Evaluating a reinforcement learning policy requires estimating the returns it can produce, but a prediction without reliable uncertainty can be misleading. This paper constructs prediction intervals for infinite-horizon returns, covering both evaluation of the policy that generated the data and evaluation of a different policy. It combines distributional reinforcement learning with conformal calibration to make those intervals distribution-free.

The central difficulties are that complete infinite-horizon returns cannot be observed, sequential observations are dependent, and changing policies changes the data distribution. The method constructs substitute returns from truncated rollouts and calibrates them using a time-aware procedure involving experience replay and weighted subsampling. These components reduce model bias and restore approximate exchangeability, a property needed for the calibration strategy.

The theoretical coverage guarantees account for model misspecification and errors in estimated importance weights. Experiments in synthetic environments and benchmarks including Mountain Car report better coverage and reliability than standard distributional reinforcement learning baselines. The result concerns trustworthy return intervals under these complications, with approximate exchangeability explicitly part of the approach.
neurips-2025-conformal-prediction-beyond.tldr: A conformal framework produces calibrated intervals for infinite-horizon policy returns while accounting for temporal dependence, model errors, and policy shifts.

paragraphs: The paper studies adapting black-box predictors from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain without access to the source data or source model. Existing approaches often emphasize reliable target samples and suppress information from unreliable ones. The authors identify two consequences: concentrating too strongly on reliable samples can cause premature overfitting, and discarding unreliable samples can lose useful information.

Their method, CVH-TDN, uses a thalamus-driven decoupling network to control the direction of sample generation in feature space. Here, visual hallucination refers to generated feature-space samples that help explore relationships among representations. The method organizes this process into three components: Hallucination Generation, Hallucination Alignment, and Hallucination Calibration. Together, they examine spatial relationships between observed samples and generated hallucinations.

This approach aims to extract information from the arrangement of samples rather than relying excessively on the most trustworthy examples. The authors report state-of-the-art performance on four standard benchmarks. Those findings support controlled feature generation as a useful strategy for this restricted domain-adaptation setting.
neurips-2025-controlled-visual-hallucina.tldr: CVH-TDN uses controlled feature-space sample generation to improve black-box domain adaptation, reporting state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks.

paragraphs: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning reduces the number of parameters needed to adapt a large model. Methods such as LoRA nevertheless adapt layers independently, so their trainable parameter count grows with model depth. This paper investigates whether adaptations across layers contain shared structure that makes separate treatment unnecessarily expensive.

The authors provide theoretical and empirical evidence that transformer skip connections encourage gradients to vary smoothly across layers. Corresponding weight updates concentrate much of their energy in low-frequency spectral components, particularly along the layer dimension. CrossSpectra captures this structure by collecting attention-weight adaptations for queries, keys, and values across layers into a single three-dimensional tensor. It represents that tensor using sparse spectral coefficients and retains only a limited set of frequencies across layers.

Its parameter count scales with the product of two spectral budgets rather than LoRA’s combination of depth, rank, and width. Across language and vision benchmarks, it matches or exceeds baseline performance with fewer parameters. In one LLaMA-7B instruction-following setting, it uses just 0.36% of LoRA’s parameter count.
neurips-2025-crossspectra-exploiting-cro.tldr: CrossSpectra compresses fine-tuning updates across transformer layers using sparse spectral representations, matching or improving baseline performance with far fewer parameters.

paragraphs: Bayesian networks describe dependencies among variables using directed acyclic graphs. When a network contains tens of thousands of variables, fitting the full model and then removing irrelevant variables can become computationally prohibitive. Estimation-collapsibility identifies cases where fitting a smaller submodel directly still permits exact inference about the target variables.

Checking that property presents two difficulties. Existing criteria require expensive searches and repeated vertex removals. They also assume a fully directed graph, whereas practical learning often identifies only a class of graphs with equivalent dependency information. That class is represented by a completed partially directed acyclic graph, or CPDAG. The paper introduces sequential c-simplicial sets to characterize estimation-collapsibility directly in this representation.

The resulting DSCS algorithm verifies the property without requiring the problem to be expressed solely through a fully specified directed graph. Numerical experiments demonstrate efficiency and scalability in high-dimensional networks. The practical value is identifying when a smaller fitted model can preserve exact target inference, rather than assuming that dropping variables is always harmless.
neurips-2025-dscs-fast-cpdag-based-verif.tldr: DSCS efficiently checks when a smaller Bayesian-network model preserves exact target inference, working directly with partially directed graph representations.

paragraphs: Speech foundation models can lose accuracy when deployed with unfamiliar background noise or speaker accents. Test-time adaptation addresses this without source data or labels, but methods using backpropagation require substantial memory. Existing alternatives developed mainly for vision can be inaccurate on speech because the task structure, noise, and model architectures differ.

The paper introduces E-BAT, a framework designed specifically for speech adaptation without backpropagation. It uses lightweight prompt adaptation to align features through forward passes. A multi-scale loss captures distribution changes at both the whole-utterance and token levels. An exponential moving average mechanism stabilizes adaptation across utterances, helping the method handle variation at multiple scales without relying on memory-intensive backward computation.

Experiments cover four noisy speech datasets and sixteen acoustic conditions. The authors report accuracy gains of 4.1%–13.5% over backpropagation-free baselines, alongside 2.0–6.4 times GPU memory savings relative to backpropagation-based methods. These are comparisons against different baseline groups: together, they support the framework’s intended balance between adaptation accuracy and memory efficiency.
neurips-2025-e-bats-efficient-backpropag.tldr: E-BAT adapts speech models without backpropagation, improving accuracy over forward-only baselines while using less memory than backpropagation-based methods.

paragraphs: Training large transformers across multiple GPUs involves communication as well as computation. Under tensor parallelism, the connection between each block’s attention module and its multilayer perceptron requires an all-reduce operation. This paper investigates whether that repeated connection can be bypassed while still giving the model a useful signal.

The proposed FAL architecture sends the first layer’s attention output to the multilayer perceptron inputs of later layers. Reusing that signal eliminates the usual per-block attention-to-perceptron connections and their associated all-reduce communication. It also permits attention and perceptron computation to execute in parallel on a single GPU. A second version, FAL+, combines normalized first-layer attention output with later attention outputs to enrich the input and improve model quality.

In the reported evaluation, FAL reduces multi-GPU training time by up to 44% and improves single-GPU throughput by up to 1.18 times while achieving better perplexity than the GPT baseline. FAL+ achieves still lower perplexity without exceeding the baseline’s training time. The results show that architectural information routing can improve both training efficiency and measured language-model quality.
neurips-2025-first-attentions-last-bette.tldr: FAL reuses first-layer attention across later layers to reduce communication and enable parallel computation, improving training speed and perplexity in evaluations.

paragraphs: Planning for continuous-time systems often uses small discrete simulation steps to maintain accuracy. Looking far ahead then requires many planning steps, making the search expensive and potentially reducing solution quality. The paper addresses this mismatch between the short timescale needed for simulation and the longer timescale useful for decision-making.

Its approach makes action duration a continuous optimization variable alongside the action itself. The planner therefore chooses both what to do and how long to do it. These temporally extended actions allow a shallow planning search to cover many primitive action steps and speed up trajectory simulation. In model-based reinforcement learning, the approach also reduces accumulating model-learning errors and improves model training time.

The authors further use a multi-armed bandit formulation to select the range of action durations automatically within the learning framework. Experiments in planning and model-based reinforcement learning report faster planning and better solutions. They also show solutions to problems left unsolved by the standard formulation, supporting action duration as a useful part of the planning decision.
neurips-2025-improving-planning-and-mbrl.tldr: Optimizing action duration alongside action choice enables faster, longer-reaching planning and improves model-based reinforcement learning in experiments.

paragraphs: Strategic classification studies decisions made about people who can modify their features to influence an outcome. This makes fairness depend on the interaction between a classifier and people’s responses to it. The paper focuses on individual fairness, an aspect that has received less attention in this setting than fairness between groups.

The authors analyze threshold-based classifiers and prove that deterministic thresholds violate individual fairness in the setting they study. They then investigate randomized classifiers, introducing conditions sufficient to ensure individual fairness. Those conditions become constraints in a linear programming problem, allowing them to find an optimal randomized classifier that also satisfies the fairness requirements. Randomization is thus paired with explicit mathematical conditions rather than treated as automatically fair.

The approach can also be extended to group fairness notions. Experiments on real-world datasets show reduced unfairness and an improved fairness–accuracy trade-off. The contribution connects a theoretical problem with deterministic thresholds to a constructive optimization method, showing how fairness requirements can guide classifier design when people respond strategically.
neurips-2025-individual-fairness-in-stra.tldr: The paper derives conditions for individually fair randomized classifiers and uses linear programming to optimize them in strategic classification settings.

paragraphs: Advertising decisions are difficult to evaluate because an advertisement’s effect may arrive later, depend on earlier exposures, and vary across customers. Repeated exposure can reinforce an advertisement’s influence or produce fatigue. This paper develops a bidding framework that addresses these delayed, cumulative, and personalized effects together.

The authors model bidding as a contextual Markov decision process with delayed Poisson rewards. This supplies a specific statistical structure for learning from delayed outcomes while accounting for customer context and sequential decisions. They propose a two-stage maximum likelihood estimator with data splitting. Its error analysis explicitly tracks how inaccuracies in the first estimation stage affect the overall estimate, providing controlled estimation error within the proposed framework.

A reinforcement learning algorithm then uses these estimates to develop personalized bidding strategies. The authors establish a near-optimal regret bound scaling as dH²√T, up to logarithmic factors, where d is context dimension, H is the number of rounds, and T is the number of customers. Simulation experiments support the theoretical findings under the modeled advertising setting.
neurips-2025-learning-personalized-ad-im.tldr: A contextual reinforcement learning framework models delayed and cumulative advertising effects to learn personalized bidding strategies with a near-optimal regret bound.

paragraphs: Training a large language model requires optimizing a large collection of weights reliably. POET approaches this challenge by changing how those weights are represented during optimization. Instead of treating the weight representation as unrestricted, it reparameterizes each neuron using two learnable orthogonal matrices together with a fixed random weight matrix.

The key mathematical feature is that these orthogonal transformations provably preserve the spectral properties of the weight matrices. Training can therefore change the learned representation while maintaining this structure. The authors connect that preservation to stable optimization of the training objective and improved generalization. The proposed benefit comes from constraining the form of learning, with the fixed random matrix and learnable transformations playing distinct roles.

To make the approach practical for large networks, the paper also develops efficient approximations of the training method. These are intended to provide flexibility and scalability beyond the basic formulation. Extensive language-model training experiments support POET’s effectiveness and scalability, presenting structured reparameterization as a promising way to improve the training process itself.
neurips-2025-reparameterized-llm-trainin.tldr: POET trains language models through learnable orthogonal transformations that preserve weight-matrix spectral properties, supporting stable optimization and improved generalization.

paragraphs: Graph condensation synthesizes a smaller graph that retains useful information from a larger one. This paper examines what happens when the original graph has been corrupted. The authors observe substantial performance deterioration and find that existing robust graph-learning techniques offer only limited help for the condensation process.

Their empirical and theoretical analysis characterizes condensation as reducing intrinsic dimension and producing a graph with lower classification complexity. That simplification is important for effective condensation, but adversarial perturbations can undermine it. The proposed MRGC framework addresses this geometrically. Three graph-manifold learning modules guide the condensed graph toward a smooth, low-dimensional structure with little ambiguity between classes.

The aim is to preserve the useful reduction in classification complexity even when the input graph is attacked. The authors describe robustness under universal adversarial attacks and report extensive experiments across diverse attack scenarios. The central contribution is a link between the geometry that makes condensation effective and the geometry that needs protection, giving robustness an explicit role in constructing the smaller graph.
neurips-2025-robust-graph-condensation-v.tldr: MRGC improves graph-condensation robustness by preserving a smooth, low-dimensional structure with low class ambiguity under adversarial perturbations.

paragraphs: A language-model router usually sends each query to one model. That can limit performance on questions that benefit from several models’ complementary strengths. Router-R1 treats routing and answer aggregation as a sequence of decisions, allowing the system to use information gained from one model when deciding what to do next.

The router is itself a language model. It alternates between internal deliberation and calls to other models, adding each response to its evolving context. Reinforcement learning trains this behavior using a lightweight reward that combines formatting, final-answer quality, and cost. Including cost makes the expense of model calls part of the learned decision process rather than leaving performance as the only objective.

Routing decisions use simple model descriptions, including pricing, latency, and example performance. The authors report strong generalization to selecting previously unseen models. Across seven general and multi-hop question-answering benchmarks, Router-R1 outperforms several strong baselines while maintaining cost management. The results support learning when to consult additional models and how to combine their contributions.
neurips-2025-router-r1-teaching-llms-mul.tldr: Router-R1 learns to alternate reasoning with multiple model calls, combining responses while balancing answer quality and cost.

paragraphs: Measuring how cells respond to chemicals often requires techniques that capture different biological signals. Some destroy the cells, preventing measurements from being paired on the same individual cell. scGeneScope addresses this by matching single-cell RNA sequencing and Cell Painting microscopy data through chemical treatment under coordinated experimental conditions.

The dataset applies 28 chemicals with distinct pathways or mechanisms of action to U2-OS cells in two experimental rounds. Matched sets of replicates are profiled independently using the two techniques. The resulting benchmark separates data by replicate and experiment to test treatment identification under laboratory variability, simulating mechanism-of-action discovery. It compares single-modality, multimodal, and multiple-profile models, from linear methods to foundation models.

Combining multiple profiles improves performance in both single-modality and multimodal settings, with more consistent gains in the former. For mechanism-of-action identification, zero-shot RNA-sequencing foundation models are consistently outperformed by classic methods fitted to the data. The released dataset and code therefore provide both an integration resource and evidence that realistic evaluation can challenge assumptions about foundation-model advantages.
neurips-2025-scgenescope-a-treatment-mat.tldr: scGeneScope pairs cellular imaging and RNA data by treatment, enabling realistic benchmarks that reveal benefits from profile integration and weaknesses in zero-shot foundation models.

paragraphs: A pretrained diffusion model connects random noise to a clean generated sample. Distillation can accelerate generation by learning improved trajectories between these endpoints. This paper examines two approaches to that goal: consistency-model distillation, which regulates trajectories through consistent projection functions, and rectified flow, which makes trajectories straight to enable faster sampling.

Each approach leaves a concern. Sampling efficiency remains an issue for consistency models, while rectified flow relies on numerical differential-equation solvers that may introduce approximation errors. SCoT aims to combine the useful properties of both by learning trajectories that are simultaneously straight and consistent. Its training balances two objectives: regulating the mapping function’s gradient to a constant and enforcing consistency along trajectories.

This formulation makes trajectory shape and trajectory consistency joint targets in the same distilled model. The intended benefit is faster sampling through a construction that incorporates both principles. Extensive experiments support SCoT’s effectiveness and efficiency. The paper’s contribution is the unified trajectory formulation, together with empirical evidence that the two properties can be productively combined.
neurips-2025-scot-unifying-consistency-m.tldr: SCoT accelerates generative sampling by distilling trajectories that jointly satisfy straightness and consistency objectives.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can struggle with three-dimensional spatial questions even after specialized training and lengthy reasoning. The paper argues that a key issue is implicit reasoning: models may discuss spatial relationships without maintaining a shared, explicit representation of the scene. SpatialReasoner introduces such a representation across perception, computation, and reasoning.

The shared three-dimensional representation gives these stages a coherent interface. What the model perceives can be carried into subsequent calculations and reasoning steps in a consistent form. This connects the scene-parsing abilities of visual foundation models with language-model reasoning. It also makes intermediate representations available for analysis, allowing the authors to examine factual errors and identify weaknesses in multi-step reasoning.

SpatialReasoner improves performance across several spatial-reasoning benchmarks and exceeds Gemini 2.0 by a reported 9.2% on 3DSRBench. It also generalizes better to novel types of three-dimensional questions. The findings support explicit representations as a way to improve both spatial reasoning and the visibility of errors within that reasoning process.
neurips-2025-spatialreasoner-towards-exp.tldr: SpatialReasoner shares explicit 3D representations across perception, computation, and reasoning, improving benchmark performance and generalization to new spatial questions.

paragraphs: Instruction tuning commonly uses responses written by people or generated by other models. Those responses can differ from the target model’s pretrained distribution, and the paper argues that this mismatch can produce diminishing returns or harm performance and robustness. GRAPE tests the hypothesis that supervision works better when it fits the model being trained.

For each instruction, GRAPE gathers candidate responses from several sources and selects the one with the highest alignment to the target model’s pretrained distribution, measured through normalized probability. It then applies ordinary supervised fine-tuning to the selected responses. The intervention lies in choosing supervision, making the same pool of candidate answers usable in a model-specific way.

Controlled experiments across multiple model families report gains over strong baselines, including distillation from the strongest model, with improvements up to 13.8% averaged across benchmarks. Benefits also extend to existing tuning datasets: selected subsets outperform baselines using substantially more data. These results support distributional fit as a useful selection principle for improving both the efficiency and effectiveness of instruction tuning.
neurips-2025-the-best-instruction-tuning.tldr: GRAPE improves instruction tuning by selecting responses that fit the target model’s pretrained distribution, often outperforming baselines trained on more data.

paragraphs: Recommender systems infer preferences from past interactions between users and items. Recent methods use language-model reasoning to improve rating predictions, often transferring reasoning from a teacher model. This paper identifies weaknesses in that process: teachers may lack recommendation skill, supervision can be expensive and static, and the transferred reasoning may remain superficial.

RecZero trains a single language model through reinforcement learning to develop reasoning for rating prediction. A structured prompt guides it through user interests, item features, and compatibility between the user and item. Rule-based rewards and group relative policy optimization train the resulting reasoning trajectories. The framework thus makes recommendation reasoning part of what the model learns through reward-driven optimization.

The authors also introduce RecOne, which first uses supervised fine-tuning on initial reasoning examples and then applies reinforcement learning. Both approaches significantly outperform existing baselines on multiple benchmark datasets. The findings support reinforcement learning as an effective route to reasoning-enhanced rating prediction, with successful results from both a purely reinforcement-learning approach and a supervised-plus-reinforcement-learning variant.
neurips-2025-think-before-recommendation.tldr: RecZero trains a single language model to reason before predicting ratings, while RecOne combines initial supervised reasoning training with reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Transform-based tensor models use algebraic structure that ordinary real-valued differential geometry does not naturally capture. This paper develops an initial geometric framework for tensors whose tube-wise multiplication is defined through orthogonal transforms. The goal is to describe their geometry in a way that respects the operations used by the models themselves.

The central construction is a smooth t-manifold, a space locally represented by structured tensor modules over a commutative t-scalar ring. Within that framework, the authors define metrics, gradients, Laplacians, and geodesics consistently with the transform-based algebra. This provides a common language for relating discrete tensor representations to continuous geometric objects and operations.

The paper then develops a statistical test for whether tensor data lie near a low-dimensional t-manifold and gives finite-sample guarantees for fitting such manifolds under noise. It also establishes approximation bounds for tensor neural networks learning smooth functions on these spaces. Their generalization rates depend on intrinsic geometric complexity, connecting the structure of the data to theoretical learning performance.
neurips-2025-towards-a-geometric-underst.tldr: The paper builds a transform-compatible geometry for tensor learning, with guarantees for noisy manifold fitting and neural-network approximation.

paragraphs: Tracking three-dimensional motion from a single video requires separating movement of the camera from movement of objects. The authors identify another weakness in existing methods: they cannot densely track dynamic subjects that appear later in the video. TrackingWorld addresses both problems with a pipeline that represents trajectories in a world-centered coordinate system.

The pipeline first turns sparse two-dimensional tracks into dense tracks using a tracking upsampler. Applying this upsampler to every frame lets the system include newly emerging objects. Tracks from overlapping regions are then removed to reduce redundancy. Finally, an optimization framework estimates camera poses and three-dimensional coordinates, converting the dense image-space tracks into trajectories expressed in a shared world coordinate frame.

This organization combines broad pixel coverage with an explicit treatment of camera motion. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate accurate, dense three-dimensional tracking. The claim is tracking almost all pixels, with particular attention to subjects entering after the initial frames, rather than restricting the tracked set to objects already visible at the beginning.
neurips-2025-trackingworld-world-centric.tldr: TrackingWorld converts dense video tracks into world-centered 3D trajectories while accounting for camera motion and newly appearing objects.

paragraphs: Regression models used in recommendation can suffer from retransformation bias when predictions are mapped back from a transformed scale. The paper argues that this problem has received insufficient attention in recommender systems. Existing corrections from other fields operate after prediction and outside the model, creating practical difficulties in large recommendation applications.

TranSUN addresses the bias within the model through a small refinement and joint bias learning. The authors provide a theoretical unbiasedness guarantee and report favorable empirical convergence. They then generalize the approach into a regression-model family called Generalized TranSUN. This broader formulation provides additional theoretical insight and a framework for constructing different models designed to avoid retransformation bias.

Experiments across data from several domains demonstrate the proposed methods’ superiority in the reported comparisons. The methods have also been deployed for product and short-video recommendations in the Taobao app’s homepage recommendation business, serving major online traffic. The contribution therefore combines an internal bias-correction formulation, a generalized model family, and evidence of practical use in industrial recommendation.
neurips-2025-transun-a-preemptive-paradi.tldr: TranSUN learns to eliminate retransformation bias within recommendation regression models, with theoretical unbiasedness and reported industrial deployment.

paragraphs: A misinformation detector can perform well by learning superficial patterns that happen to correlate with false claims in its training data. Those shortcuts may fail when misinformation changes form, especially when language models can generate convincing text. TruthOverTricks provides a unified evaluation framework for measuring how strongly detectors depend on such cues.

The framework distinguishes intrinsic shortcut induction from extrinsic shortcut injection. It evaluates seven representative detectors on fourteen existing benchmarks and two new factual-misinformation datasets, NQ-Misinfo and Streaming-Misinfo. The experiments find severe performance degradation under both naturally occurring and deliberately crafted shortcuts. This exposes a gap between success on familiar patterns and robustness when those patterns become unreliable.

The proposed Shortcut Mitigation Framework uses language models for data augmentation through paraphrasing, factual summarization, and sentiment normalization. These transformations aim to reduce dependence on shortcut cues and promote attention to semantic content. The method consistently improves robustness across sixteen benchmarks, providing both a way to diagnose shortcut reliance and a training intervention that reduces it in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-truth-over-tricks-measuring.tldr: TruthOverTricks exposes shortcut reliance in misinformation detectors, and targeted language-model data augmentation improves robustness across sixteen benchmarks.

paragraphs: The paper asks whether language-model preferences form coherent structures that can meaningfully be studied as value systems. It uses utility functions to analyze relationships among independently sampled preferences. The authors find substantial structural coherence in current models and report that this coherence emerges with scale. They interpret these findings as evidence for meaningful emergent value systems.

Building on that analysis, the authors propose utility engineering: studying and controlling AI utilities as a research agenda. Their investigations identify troubling preference patterns despite existing control measures, including cases in which models prioritize themselves over humans or show opposition toward particular individuals. These findings concern the preferences revealed by their analysis and motivate direct attention to the structure of model utilities.

The paper also proposes methods for utility control. In a case study, aligning utilities with a citizen assembly reduces political bias and generalizes to new scenarios. The contribution combines a measurement framework, empirical findings about coherent preferences, and an intervention demonstrating that these measured utility structures can be influenced.
neurips-2025-utility-engineering-analyzi.tldr: Utility engineering analyzes coherent preferences in language models and explores controlling them, including a citizen-assembly alignment case study that reduces political bias.

paragraphs: This paper studies why diffusion models can generate useful new samples before they begin memorizing training data. It identifies two training timescales: an earlier point when high-quality generation appears and a later point when memorization emerges. The separation between these events provides a period in which a model can generalize effectively.

The authors find that the onset of memorization grows linearly with training-set size, while the onset of high-quality generation remains constant. Larger datasets therefore widen this useful training window. Continued training can still produce strong memorization beyond it. In the reported analysis, overfitting disappears even at infinite training time only when dataset size exceeds a model-dependent threshold.

The authors describe this timing effect as implicit dynamical regularization: the learning process itself delays memorization, including in highly overparameterized settings. Their evidence combines experiments using standard U-Net architectures on realistic and synthetic datasets with theory for a tractable random-features model in a high-dimensional limit. The findings explain a window of generalization rather than establishing that diffusion models never memorize.
neurips-2025-why-diffusion-models-dont-m.tldr: Diffusion models can generalize before memorizing because larger training sets delay memorization while leaving the onset of high-quality generation unchanged in the studied settings.

paragraphs: Video inpainting and editing often require substantial training resources and large datasets. ZeroPatcher investigates whether pretrained text-to-video generators already contain enough useful knowledge to perform these tasks without additional training. Its approach changes the sampling process used with the generator so that known parts of a video guide the generated result.

The proposed denoising sampler optimizes the generation trajectory by maximizing an expected log-likelihood conditioned on known video segments. This makes the available video content part of the objective guiding the trajectory. For removing or replacing moving objects, a latent mask fuser performs video masking directly in the model’s latent space, avoiding explicit decoding and re-encoding through the variational autoencoder.

The authors implement the method with CogVideoX and HunyuanVideo, providing evidence that the sampler can work across different foundation generators. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations report strong inpainting and editing performance in a plug-and-play setting. The contribution is a reusable sampling and masking procedure that applies pretrained video-generation capabilities to editing without further model training.
neurips-2025-zeropatcher-training-free-s.tldr: ZeroPatcher enables video inpainting and editing without additional training by guiding pretrained generators with a new sampler and latent-space masking.
